summary: Fourteen days of Nightscout data with 98.7 percent CGM coverage show mean glucose 121.6 mg/dL, 86 percent time in range, 8.9 percent above range, and 5.1 percent below range. Local afternoons rise, then evenings and early nights fall, including readings near 41-42 mg/dL. The selected AAPS profile is complete and declared applicable, but carbohydrate entries are zero and the user-declared meal-strategy list is empty, so UAM and SMB are the observed meal controller. Overnight basal, overnight target, afternoon basal, flat ISF, Dynamic ISF, and SMB remain competing explanations. The profile is kept and one verification plan is used before any later single change.

analysis_steps.findings: The 14-day window has 3995 valid CGM readings, about 5-minute cadence, 98.7 percent coverage, 10 gaps, largest gap 65 minutes, and no invalid or duplicate points. Insulin treatments total 275.95 U across 655 insulin entries. Carbohydrate entries are 0 g. The selected AAPS profile includes basal, CR, flat ISF, targets, DIA 10 h, and the six AAPS setting groups. Historical applicability is declared yes. The first calendar day is partial.
analysis_steps.evidence: CGM coverage 98.7 percent, 3995 of 4046 expected points, 2315 treatments, complete selected profile, empty carb list.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No meal composition. Dilution or U200 conversion is not quantified. Pre-13 Aug versus post-switch settings are not stored as a second profile. Loop statuses are a 24-row sample, not the full device-status stream.

analysis_steps.findings: TBR 5.1 percent exceeds a common 4 percent review mark and clusters locally at 01:00 (18.5 percent), 19:00 (15.3 percent), and around midnight. Lows reach 41-42 mg/dL. TAR concentrates from late morning through 16:00 (mean 162.8 mg/dL, TAR 32.1 percent). CV is 32.6 percent. Events include GLP-1 notes, site and sensor changes, and an occlusion with pump error on 19 Aug. Sampled IOB already reached about 4.7-5.9 U at peaks. This hypoglycemia pattern limits later insulin-increasing ideas.
analysis_steps.evidence: Overall TIR/TAR/TBR, local hourly TBR and TAR, glucose extremes 41-293 mg/dL, safety events, sampled IOB at high glucose.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Requires adequate CGM coverage from data_quality.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No activity log. Exercise, alcohol, GLP-1, occlusion, and dilution cannot be separated from insulin effect.

analysis_steps.findings: Scheduled basal is 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.7, 0.5, 0.6, then 0.7 U/h and sums near 16 U/day. Local 04:00-08:00 is the most stable window. Overnight 00:00-03:00 has high TBR despite modest averages. The lowest basal (0.5 U/h at 16:00) sits under the highest TAR, but that window also matches unannounced intake and UAM. Targets are 90 mg/dL overnight and after 23:00, and 100 mg/dL from 08:00. Afternoon highs and evening lows are not labeled as isolated basal defects.
analysis_steps.evidence: Local hourly averages and TBR/TAR, basal and target segments, correction-response drops after afternoon insulin, 13 Aug profile-switch notes.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Safety TBR and TAR constrain any basal or target change. Meal versus basal effects are not separated.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No fasting-only or skipped-meal flags. Temp basal and SMB dominate delivery, so scheduled basal is only part of insulin action.

analysis_steps.findings: CR segments exist (13, 11.1, 13.2, 10.5, 12.6 g/U) but were not used because carbs and COB stayed at zero. ISF is flat 56 mg/dL/U while Dynamic ISF is on; sampled variable sensitivity ranged widely below and above 56. DIA is 10 h, which can carry afternoon insulin into evening and overnight lows. Correction windows are not dose-proportional and cannot validate ISF 56. CR inference is blocked. ISF and DIA remain entangled with SMB and Dynamic ISF.
analysis_steps.evidence: Zero carb treatments, COB 0 in sampled statuses, flat ISF 56, DIA 10 h, variable_sens about 28-124 mg/dL/U, mixed 2-6 hour glucose changes after small corrections.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Basal and target hypotheses stay open. Safety TBR forbids treating ISF 56 as too weak.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No logged meals, so CR cannot be tested. True ISF cannot be isolated from basal, SMB, UAM, and unknown carbs. Insulin peak is not numerically specified beyond free-peak oref.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are on, always-on SMB is on, COB and after-carb SMB are off, SMB with ordinary temp targets is on, and SMB with high temp targets is off. That matches zero carbs and repeated temp targets of 135 mg/dL. Configured interval is 3 minutes with 15/20 minute SMB and UAM caps, but sampled reasons include UAM boosts and microboluses that can exceed those inventory caps. Automation is compensating for missing meal announcement and is a plausible contributor to afternoon stacking then evening lows.
analysis_steps.evidence: AAPS SMB groups, COB 0, temp targets at 135 mg/dL, sampled SMB amounts including a 1.6 U UAM high boost, afternoon TAR then 19:00 TBR.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Safety hypoglycemia gate. Unresolved basal, ISF, DIA, and meal explanations.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Full 6214 device-status stream not reviewed. Custom boost logic is only visible in sampled reasons.

analysis_steps.findings: Autosens is off and Dynamic ISF is on at 70 percent, with Autosens target raise and lower off. A sensitivity_ratio of 1 is a neutral snapshot, not disabled Autosens. Max basal 12 U/h and max IOB 25 U did not bind; sampled high-end clip was about 4 U/h maxSafeBasal and peak IOB about 6 U. Carb-absorption settings are inert with COB 0. Dynamic ISF on a strong flat ISF 56 can add insulin at peaks and is not separable from SMB. Unused ceilings are not the first review target.
analysis_steps.evidence: Autosens off, Dynamic ISF 70 percent, variable_sens falling near 28-38 mg/dL/U at 245-262 mg/dL, insulinReq still positive with IOB 4.7-5.9 U, maxSafeBasal about 4 U/h.
analysis_steps.dependencies: ISF 56, DIA 10 h, SMB/UAM, and unlogged meals can all produce the same high-then-low shape.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No Autosens time-course because Autosens is disabled. Carb-absorption settings have no meal-linked test.

analysis_steps.findings: User-declared meal_strategies is an empty list and strategy_stable_for_period is null, so there is no declared prebolus or immediate-bolus percent to reproduce. Telemetry shows only correction boluses and temp basals, not meal boluses. Observed execution is unannounced daytime rises handled by UAM/SMB, sometimes after a 135 mg/dL temp target. Declared strategy and observed execution therefore cannot be compared beyond that empty declaration.
analysis_steps.evidence: Empty meal_strategies, zero carb entries, 24 correction-only response windows, temp targets at 135 mg/dL, no meal-bolus treatments.
analysis_steps.dependencies: CR unused. SMB/UAM and high temp-target flags are the actual meal actuators. Overnight hypoglycemia risk limits any guessed full bolus.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Absent declared prebolus_minutes and immediate_bolus_percent. No meal-linked bolus timing.

analysis_steps.findings: There are no e-carb amounts, start offsets, or durations. Extended carb entries are zero. UAM is not e-carbs and is not a pump extended bolus. Absorption model values cannot be tested. No e-carb pattern is attributed to profile or automation.
analysis_steps.evidence: Empty carb_treatment_entries, extended_carb_entries 0, COB 0, inert min_5m_carbimpact 8 and meal_max_absorption_hours 7.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Meal-bolus strategy is undeclared. Introducing e-carbs on top of UAM would mix COB with existing SMB.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Absent e-carb amount, offset, and duration fields.

analysis_steps.findings: Most likely shared mechanism is unannounced daytime intake plus UAM/SMB and Dynamic ISF, then 10 h DIA leftover into target 90 and overnight TBR. Weaker alternatives are a slightly high 00:00-03:00 basal or a slightly low 16:00 basal. Mid-period profile switch, GLP-1, occlusion, and dilute or U200 notes lower confidence in any one parameter. Package data override earlier temptation to change ISF from a TDD rule of thumb or to treat afternoon TAR as a proven basal defect. Conservative sequence: keep the full profile, observe meal-start time and temp-target use, then consider only one later family if lows persist on low-IOB nights. Do not change basal, target, ISF, Dynamic ISF, and SMB together.
analysis_steps.evidence: Combined glucose-by-hour pattern, zero carbs, empty meal declaration, sampled IOB and Dynamic ISF, safety TBR, decision inventory completeness.
analysis_steps.dependencies: All prior stages. Unresolved meal versus profile versus automation confounding.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: The single highest-value missing observation is clock time of usual daytime eating plus whether a 135 mg/dL temp target and extra insulin were used.

strengths: CGM coverage is 98.7 percent with good data quality, so time-of-day patterns are readable.
Overall time in range is 86 percent with mean glucose 121.6 mg/dL.
Local 04:00-08:00 is highly stable, which argues against a broad overnight basal failure.
The selected profile is complete and declared applicable for the period.
High temp targets of 135 mg/dL were used and match SMB-with-high-temp-target set to false.
The loop sometimes set zero or low temp basal when predicted guard glucose was low.
issues: Time below range is 5.1 percent and clusters in the evening and early night, with nadirs near 41-42 mg/dL.
Afternoon time above range peaks near 16:00 and is not separable from unlogged intake.
No carbohydrate entries and an empty declared meal-strategy list leave CR unused and make UAM the meal controller.
Sampled IOB of about 5-6 U at peaks, Dynamic ISF, and 10 h DIA can explain late overshoot.
A 13 Aug profile switch, GLP-1 notes, a 19 Aug occlusion, and dilute or U200 labeling reduce period homogeneity.

recommendations.title: Keep the profile and verify overnight lows against leftover IOB
recommendations.description: The primary safe action is no profile change. Evening and 00:00-03:00 lows can come from afternoon UAM or correction stacks and 10 h DIA rather than from 0.6 U/h overnight basal or the 90 mg/dL overnight target. Local 04:00-08:00 is already stable. Raising afternoon basal, cutting overnight basal, raising ISF, and tightening SMB would all target the same unresolved shape.

suggested_change.first_step: Compare several nights with versus without a prior afternoon rise or correction stack before discussing any single later change.

recommendations.title: Leave SMB, UAM, and Dynamic ISF unchanged while collecting meal timing
recommendations.description: Automation is compensating for zero carb entries. Changing SMB interval, UAM minutes, or Dynamic ISF now would confound the overnight basal versus IOB question. High temp target 135 mg/dL is already the observed way to pause SMB.

suggested_change.review_direction: Do not adjust automation in the same step as any later profile review.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep every current basal, target, CR, ISF, and DIA value. Next action is a verification plan, not a setting change: review 00:00-03:00 lows on nights with low leftover IOB versus nights after an afternoon UAM or correction stack.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Overnight TBR is the safety constraint, but 04:00-08:00 is excellent and carbs were never logged, so the same pattern can be leftover insulin rather than excess 00:00 basal 0.6 U/h or a weak 16:00 basal 0.5 U/h. Flat ISF 56 and Dynamic ISF are also open. Package evidence does not isolate one profile segment with enough confidence to change it.
profile_recommendation.next_check: For 3-5 nights record last afternoon rise or correction time, approximate IOB near 23:00, whether a 135 mg/dL temp target was used, and 00:00-03:00 low time.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: local 00:00-03:00 TBR is high, but 04:00-08:00 is stable and afternoon insulin plus 10 h DIA can still be active. Uncertainty: no fasting-only nights. Dependencies: overnight target 90, SMB always on, and residual IOB. A cut would stack with those other explanations.

Evidence: local 05:00-07:00 time in range is 95-99 percent with little TAR. Uncertainty: one 42 mg/dL reading near 07:19 local on 21 Aug. Dependencies: nearby 06:00 basal and overnight IOB. No isolated defect.

Evidence: this is the highest basal, yet mornings are the flattest high-TIR window. Uncertainty: it may be leftover dawn coverage, but lowering it is unsupported while 04:00-08:00 is already good. Dependencies: 05:00 and 10:00 segments and morning target 100 from 08:00.

Evidence: TAR rises from late morning, with COB 0 and UAM active. Uncertainty: meals versus basal are not separated. Dependencies: CR unused, SMB/UAM, Dynamic ISF. Do not raise this segment as a meal substitute.

Evidence: 16:00 has the highest TAR and the lowest basal, but the same hours show unannounced rises and later 19:00 TBR. Uncertainty: raising 0.5 U/h could add to UAM stacks. Dependencies: 18:00 basal, SMB/UAM, DIA 10 h. Keep until meal timing is known.

Evidence: local 18:00-19:00 is the crash window after afternoon highs, not a fasting rise. Uncertainty: activity and GLP-1 are unmeasured. Dependencies: prior 16:00 basal, leftover SMB, target 90 later at night. No increase and no isolated cut.

Evidence: 19:00 local TBR is 15.3 percent. Uncertainty: this may be IOB, not a 0.7 U/h defect. Dependencies: overnight 00:00 basal and target 90. Changing this together with overnight basal would double-count.

Evidence: CR was not used; carb entries are 0 and COB is 0. Uncertainty: no meal test. Dependencies: UAM/SMB is the observed controller. An empty meal_strategies list is an absent declaration, not a reason to invent a new CR.
Evidence: no carb-linked doses in this segment. Uncertainty: breakfast, if any, is unlogged. Dependencies: morning basal stability and UAM. Keep the existing 11.1 g/U.
Evidence: daytime TAR occurs with COB 0, so this CR was not exercised. Uncertainty: cannot call 13.2 g/U too weak or too strong. Dependencies: SMB always on and Dynamic ISF. Keep.

Evidence: strongest scheduled CR sits under the highest TAR, which argues against a simple too-weak CR story when carbs are unlogged. Uncertainty: no meal sizes. Dependencies: afternoon UAM and 16:00 basal. Keep.
Evidence: evening is a hypoglycemia window, not a missed meal-bolus test of 12.6 g/U. Uncertainty: dinner announcement unknown. Dependencies: DIA 10 h and overnight target. Keep.

Evidence: flat 56 plus Dynamic ISF produced much lower effective sensitivity at peaks, and large late drops followed clustered insulin. Uncertainty: corrections are confounded by unknown carbs and SMB. Dependencies: Dynamic ISF 70 percent, DIA 10 h, TBR gate. Do not weaken or strengthen ISF in the same step as automation.

Evidence: overnight target 90 coincides with 00:00-03:00 TBR, but leftover IOB is a competing cause. Uncertainty: no low-IOB fasting night set. Dependencies: 23:00 target 90, always-on SMB, 00:00 basal. Keep now; this is a candidate for a later single review only if lows persist without afternoon stacks.

Evidence: daytime target 100 sits over mixed TAR that is more consistent with unannounced intake than with a target that is too high. Uncertainty: temp targets of 135 overlay this segment. Dependencies: SMB-with-high-temp-target false. Keep.

Evidence: 23:00 returns to 90 as late-evening TBR begins. Uncertainty: same IOB confound as the 00:00 target. Dependencies: 00:00 target and overnight basal. Do not change both targets and basal together.

Evidence: 10 h DIA can keep afternoon insulin on board into evening lows; shortening it could hide IOB and add insulin. Uncertainty: insulin type is free-peak oref without a numeric peak. Dependencies: ISF, Dynamic ISF, SMB. Keep.

Evidence: with zero carbs, UAM is the meal detector and turning it off would leave afternoon rises unhandled unless meals are announced. Uncertainty: UAM also contributes to evening stacks. Dependencies: empty meal declaration and CR unused. Keep while collecting meal timing. No source component is null, so verify is not used.

Evidence: COB and after-carb flags off match cob 0. High-temp-target SMB off matches repeated 135 mg/dL temp targets. Uncertainty: always-on SMB can still dose toward overnight target 90. Dependencies: meal announcement and overnight target. Keep the existing activation set.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: 3-minute cadence and UAM boosts can stack on afternoon rises; sampled SMB sometimes exceeded the 15/20 minute inventory story. Uncertainty: Dynamic ISF may be the stronger peak actuator. Dependencies: ISF, DIA, maxSafeBasal. Do not tighten delivery in the same step as a profile change.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: 12 U/h and 25 U did not bind; sampled clip was about 4 U/h and peak IOB about 6 U. Uncertainty: lowering unused ceilings may do nothing until actuators change. Dependencies: SMB and Dynamic ISF. Keep these unused limits rather than treating them as the first safety lever.

Evidence: Autosens is off, so a sensitivity_ratio of 1 is not an Autosens diagnosis. Dynamic ISF 70 percent with ISF 56 can explain strong peak dosing. Uncertainty: it may also be compensating for unlogged meals. Dependencies: profile ISF and SMB. Keep; do not enable Autosens or change the 70 percent factor until meals and profile are separated.
Evidence: both values are inert with 0 g carbs and COB 0. Uncertainty: no absorption curve exists. Dependencies: empty e-carb fields. Keep; do not infer a duration from an average.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: There is no declared prebolus, immediate-bolus percent, or e-carb plan. Keep meals unbolused or only lightly corrected until carb or meal-start records exist; if a rise is expected, use the already observed 135 mg/dL high temp target so SMB and UAM pause, then allow UAM only after that temp target ends if glucose is still rising. Do not add e-carbs or invent a prebolus or immediate-bolus percent.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: User-declared meal_strategies is empty and Nightscout carbs are zero, so observed execution is UAM/SMB on Dynamic ISF and 10 h DIA. That pattern fits afternoon highs then evening and overnight lows. High temp target 135 mg/dL is the only meal-timing tool actually used and is consistent with SMB-with-high-temp-target set to false.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: For 3-5 usual daytime eating events, record clock time, whether a 135 mg/dL temp target was set, and any insulin the user gave, even without grams.

exceptions.pattern: Recurring local 12:00-17:00 rise then evening crash
exceptions.suggestion: Prefer an eating-soon 135 mg/dL temp target before that window rather than extra chase corrections.
exceptions.rationale: Residual IOB into 18:00-01:00 is the hypoglycemia pattern and is not a CR test.

exceptions.suggestion: Treat this window as not a meal-bolus or e-carb problem and avoid late catch-up insulin against target 90.
exceptions.rationale: TBR here is more consistent with leftover IOB and overnight target than with an evening carb-ratio miss.

implementation_steps: Keep all current profile and AAPS values while CGM coverage stays good.
Record meal-start clock time, 135 mg/dL temp-target use, and any user-given insulin for several usual daytime events.
Compare 00:00-03:00 lows on nights after an afternoon stack versus nights with low leftover IOB.
If a later review is still needed, discuss only one family: either overnight target or 00:00 basal, not both, and not with ISF or SMB.
Leave SMB, UAM, Dynamic ISF, max IOB, and max basal unchanged during that single later review.
Do not add e-carbs or a guessed prebolus until carbohydrate or meal-start records exist.
If any future change is tried, change one item, wait, and watch evening and overnight glucose closely.
education: Time below range clustered after afternoon rises often means leftover insulin rather than a standalone overnight basal number.
UAM detects unexpected rises when carbs are not entered; it is not the same as COB or an extended bolus.
Dynamic ISF can make a flat ISF of 56 act much stronger at high glucose even when Autosens is off.
A 10-hour DIA means afternoon microboluses can still matter at midnight.
A high temp target of 135 mg/dL with SMB-with-high-temp-target off is a pause on SMB, not a carb entry.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only and is not medical advice.
The user must independently verify every proposed idea with their care team.
Make at most one setting change at a time and monitor glucose closely.
Readings near 41-42 mg/dL and 5.1 percent time below range limit any insulin-increasing review.
Occlusion, GLP-1 notes, site changes, and dilute or U200 labeling can change insulin delivery independently of profile numbers.
Do not change AAPS automatically from this analysis.
